natural: SELECT * FROM employees NATURAL JOIN departments
using: SELECT name, dept_name FROM employees JOIN departments USING (dept_id)
using_left: SELECT * FROM employees LEFT JOIN departments USING (dept_id)
cross: SELECT d.dept_name, p.name FROM departments d CROSS JOIN products p
comma: SELECT e.name, d.dept_name FROM employees e, departments d WHERE e.dept_id = d.dept_id
self: SELECT e.name, m.name AS boss FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id
right: SELECT d.dept_name, e.name FROM employees e RIGHT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id
full: SELECT d.dept_name, e.name FROM employees e FULL OUTER JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id
three: SELECT c.name, p.name, oi.qty FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id=o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id=oi.product_id
derived: SELECT s.dept_id, s.n FROM (SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) n FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id) AS s WHERE s.n > 1
derived_join: SELECT e.name, s.n FROM employees e JOIN (SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) n FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id) s ON s.dept_id=e.dept_id
in_sub: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE dept_id IN (SELECT dept_id FROM departments WHERE dept_name LIKE 'E%')
exists: SELECT d.dept_name FROM departments d WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees e WHERE e.dept_id = d.dept_id)
scalar: SELECT name, salary, (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) AS avg_all FROM employees
union: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE dept_id=1 UNION SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary>100000 ORDER BY 1
unionall: SELECT dept_id FROM employees UNION ALL SELECT dept_id FROM departments
intersect: SELECT dept_id FROM employees INTERSECT SELECT dept_id FROM departments
except: SELECT dept_id FROM departments EXCEPT SELECT dept_id FROM employees ORDER BY dept_id LIMIT 5
order_alias: SELECT name, salary*2 AS dbl FROM employees ORDER BY dbl DESC, name
order_ord: SELECT name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY 2 DESC, 1 LIMIT 3 OFFSET 1
star_order_ord: SELECT * FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id=d.dept_id ORDER BY 2
qstar: SELECT e.*, d.dept_name FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id=d.dept_id
case: SELECT name, CASE WHEN salary>=150000 THEN 'high' WHEN salary>=100000 THEN 'mid' ELSE 'low' END AS band FROM employees
group_alias: SELECT substr(hire_date,1,4) yr, COUNT(*) n FROM employees GROUP BY yr ORDER BY yr
group_ord: SELECT dept_id, SUM(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY 1
having_alias: SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) c FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id HAVING c >= 3
count_distinct: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT dept_id), MAX(salary), MIN(salary), group_concat(name) FROM employees
agg_nogroup_empty: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(salary) FROM employees WHERE salary > 999999
agg_where_null: SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) FROM employees WHERE manager_id <> 1 GROUP BY dept_id
win_rows: SELECT name, salary, SUM(salary) OVER (ORDER BY emp_id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) s FROM employees
win_default_ties: SELECT name, salary, SUM(salary) OVER (ORDER BY salary) s FROM employees
win_lag_lead: SELECT name, LAG(salary) OVER (ORDER BY emp_id) p, LEAD(salary, 2, 0) OVER (ORDER BY emp_id) n FROM employees
win_ntile_pr: SELECT name, NTILE(3) OVER (ORDER BY salary) t, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary) pr, CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY salary) cd FROM employees
win_first_last: SELECT name, FIRST_VALUE(name) OVER (PARTITION BY dept_id ORDER BY salary DESC) f, LAST_VALUE(name) OVER (PARTITION BY dept_id ORDER BY salary DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) l FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL
win_groups: SELECT name, salary, COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY salary GROUPS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) c FROM employees
win_range_off: SELECT name, salary, COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY salary RANGE BETWEEN 20000 PRECEDING AND 20000 FOLLOWING) c FROM employees
win_exclude: SELECT name, SUM(salary) OVER (ORDER BY emp_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW) s FROM employees
win_empty_over: SELECT name, salary, AVG(salary) OVER () FROM employees
win_named_two: SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER w r, RANK() OVER w k FROM employees WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY salary DESC)
win_expr_item: SELECT name, salary - AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY dept_id) AS diff FROM employees
cte_chain: WITH a AS (SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) n FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id), b AS (SELECT * FROM a WHERE n>1) SELECT * FROM b JOIN departments d USING (dept_id)
rec_union: WITH RECURSIVE r(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION SELECT n+1 FROM r WHERE n<5) SELECT * FROM r
rec_nums_limit: WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM c LIMIT 6) SELECT x FROM c
quoted: SELECT "name", e."salary" FROM "employees" AS e WHERE e."salary" > 100000
comments:
-- hi
SELECT name /* c */ FROM employees -- tail
WHERE salary > 1
between_and: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary BETWEEN 90000 AND 130000 AND dept_id = 2
or_where: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 1 OR salary < 70000
like_null: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE dept_id <> 1
is_distinct_from: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM 1
join_on_complex: SELECT e.name, m.name FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id AND m.salary > 100000
nonequi: SELECT a.name, b.name FROM employees a JOIN employees b ON a.salary < b.salary AND a.dept_id = b.dept_id
left_where_trap: SELECT d.dept_name, e.name FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id WHERE e.salary > 100000
fn_in_from: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT MIN(salary) FROM employees)
using_full_star: SELECT * FROM employees FULL JOIN departments USING (dept_id)
using_right_star: SELECT * FROM employees RIGHT JOIN departments USING (dept_id)
compound_offset: SELECT dept_id FROM employees UNION SELECT dept_id FROM departments ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 2 OFFSET 1
where_alias_null: SELECT name, manager_id*2 AS dbl FROM employees WHERE dbl > 2 OR dbl IS NULL
where_alias_unknown: SELECT name, manager_id + 1 AS m FROM employees WHERE m > 2
win_group_rank: SELECT dept_id, SUM(salary) s, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(salary) DESC) r FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id
win_group_pct: SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) c, ROUND(100.0*COUNT(*)/SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (),1) pct FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id HAVING COUNT(*)>1
win_implicit_agg: SELECT COUNT(*) c, SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () t FROM employees
win_group_partition: SELECT d.dept_name, p.category, SUM(oi.qty) q, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.category ORDER BY SUM(oi.qty) DESC) r FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.product_id=oi.product_id CROSS JOIN departments d GROUP BY d.dept_id, p.category
win_with_group: SELECT dept_id, SUM(salary) s, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(salary) DESC) r FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id
or_3vl: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 1 OR manager_id = 5
or_and_mix: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 1 AND salary > 130000 OR manager_id IS NULL OR name LIKE 'K%'
or_between: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary BETWEEN 90000 AND 100000 OR dept_id IS NULL
rec_union_limit: WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION SELECT x+1 FROM c LIMIT 4) SELECT x FROM c
rec_big_limit: WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM c LIMIT 100) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM c
rec_limit_hits_anchor: WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (VALUES (1),(2),(3) UNION ALL SELECT x+10 FROM c LIMIT 2) SELECT x FROM c
sub_exists: SELECT d.dept_name FROM departments d WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees e WHERE e.dept_id = d.dept_id)
sub_not_exists: SELECT d.dept_name FROM departments d WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees e WHERE e.dept_id = d.dept_id)
sub_scalar_select: SELECT d.dept_name, (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees e WHERE e.dept_id = d.dept_id) AS top FROM departments d
sub_in_correlated: SELECT e.name FROM employees e WHERE e.salary IN (SELECT MAX(x.salary) FROM employees x WHERE x.dept_id = e.dept_id)
sub_in_uncorrelated: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE dept_id IN (SELECT dept_id FROM departments WHERE dept_name LIKE 'E%')
sub_list_select: SELECT c.name, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id) AS n_orders, (SELECT MAX(o.order_date) FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id) AS last_order FROM customers c
